Per-species ranges re-used from research/asia_mainland.json (HMW 2016 ranges, ADW, Wikipedia; see that file for details), plus: C. honkhoaiensis - holotype (IEBR-M-6439, adult female) head-body 175 mm, tail 180 mm, 152 g, as reported from the original description (Nguyen, Oshida, Dang, Bui & Motokawa 2018, J. Mammal. 99: 813-825, doi:10.1093/jmammal/gyy061) by German and Catalan Wikipedia; the original paper is paywalled (OUP and ResearchGate returned 403; Wayback unreachable), so the full Hon Khoai sample range could not be read. A search-engine summary (not retrievable text, NOT used) gave 165.0-175.0 mm for the sample; either way the species lies well inside 130-300. C. melanogaster - HMW gives only means (209 mm males, 212 mm females); entered as 209-212. C. concolor - not a separate HMW account: HMW treats it as C. caniceps concolor, so it is covered by the C. caniceps range (215-222 mm). Genus min 130 and max 300 come from the weaker Wikipedia statements kept from asia_mainland (genus "13 to 27 cm", C. notatus "about 20-30 cm"), deliberately wide; the narrowest well-sourced per-species union would be 148-291 mm. Separation from Exilisciurus (62-93), Nannosciurus (62-82) and Rheithrosciurus (334-352) holds with these wide bounds.

evidence.quote: The upper incisors without extreme abnormalities; (in genera in which these teeth are becoming thickened, their anterior surfaces are without grooves).

upper_incisor_groove.notes: Ellerman (1940) key to the Sciurus group: after Rheithrosciurus (many parallel grooves) and Glyphotes are keyed out, all remaining genera, including Callosciurus s.l. (with Tamiops as subgenus and the species now in Sundasciurus/Prosciurillus/Rubrisciurus), have upper incisors "without extreme abnormalities" whose anterior surfaces are without grooves. Same evidence and standard as the island group used for Lariscus/Sundasciurus. Caveat: in his Syntheosciurus remarks Ellerman notes that "grooves may appear from time to time, as in, for instance, Heliosciurus, in other genera" (no Callosciurus case cited).

bulla_anteromesial_lobe.notes: DELIBERATE WIDENING of the island-group coding ("present", genus). The Moore (1958/1959) lobe defines Sundasciurus as it stood before 2016, but S. everetti (Bornean mountain ground squirrel, transferred from Dremomys by Hawkins et al. 2016) does not reliably show it: Moore & Tate (1965: 291) found the inflated anteromesial chamber in only 6 of 27 MCZ skulls, the rest agreeing with the other Dremomys species (single, unforked septum); Hawkins et al. (2016, Table 3) score everetti as "Intermediate" with "considerable variation". So the union over all species is {absent, present}. With S. everetti excluded, the lobe would separate Sundasciurus from Callosciurus, Tamiops, Lariscus, Menetes and Dremomys (Moore 1958, 1959; Hinckley et al. 2020 restate the genus definition as "the presence of a Y-shaped trans-bullar bony septum" and note S. rabori has an "intermediate antero-mesial lobe").

cheekteeth_pattern_lost_from_birth.notes: NEW CHARACTER (see Callosciurus). In Ellerman (1940) all Sundasciurus species then known were in Callosciurus (forms seen include brookei, fraterculus, hippurus, jentinki, juvencus, lowii, mindanensis, mollendorffi, philippinensis, samarensis, steerii, tenuis) and everetti was in Dremomys (forms seen "everetii"); both genera key out under "Cheekteeth not simplified, not losing all traces of normal pattern till adult or usually late in life", vs Lariscus. Later-described or later-split species (davensis, hoogstraali, rabori, altitudinis, tahan, robinsoni, natunensis) are covered only by this genus-level statement. Separates Sundasciurus from Lariscus.

caveats: (1) VERBATIM: all quotes marked verbatim were machine-checked (whitespace-normalised, line-end hyphenation re-joined) against the retrieved text (nannosrc_work/moore1959.txt, moore1958.txt, ellerman1940.txt, hawkins2016.txt; asia_work/mt.txt and HMW/ADW/Wikipedia texts; followup_work/wiki_de.txt, wiki_ca.txt), except two Moore & Tate (1965: 291) sentences whose OCR interleaves lines; those were checked on the rendered page image. OCR artefacts are kept as retrieved (e.g. Moore 1959 'proo"dont'). (2) SUNDASCIURUS BULLA: this file deliberately ADDS "absent" to Sundasciurus bulla_anteromesial_lobe (island file: "present", genus) because S. everetti shows the generic lobe in only 6/27 skulls (Moore & Tate 1965) and is "intermediate" (Hawkins et al. 2016). After the union, the lobe separates nothing from Sundasciurus; the "absent" codings added for Callosciurus, Tamiops, Lariscus, Menetes and Dremomys are sourced but currently non-separating. If the project ever excludes S. everetti, the lobe would separate Sundasciurus from all five. (3) KEY-LEAD EVIDENCE: several codings rest on genus keys (Moore 1959 key to the Callosciurina; Ellerman 1940 key to the Sciurus group), i.e. on which lead a genus is keyed under. Those keys predate later splits (e.g. Sundasciurus davensis/hoogstraali/rabori/altitudinis/tahan/robinsoni/natunensis, Tamiops minshanicus, Callosciurus honkhoaiensis) and the transfer of everetti from Dremomys to Sundasciurus; their characters are generic and the same standard was used by the island and mainland groups. (4) NEW CHARACTER KEYS: cheekteeth_pattern_lost_from_birth (Ellerman 1940) and occiput_median_keel_pronounced (Moore 1959) are new; all other keys reuse existing ones exactly (incisors_broad_divergent, bulla_anteromesial_lobe, p4_largest_upper_cheek_tooth, upper_incisors_reduced, teat_pairs, upper_incisor_orientation, nasal_vs_interorbital, upper_incisor_groove, hb_length_mm). (5) C. HONKHOAIENSIS SIZE: only the holotype value (HB 175 mm) could be read, via Wikipedia citing the original description; the paper itself is paywalled. It does not change the Callosciurus union (130-300 mm). (6) NOT CODED (deliberately): Menetes upper_incisors_reduced (Ellerman calls them "rather shortened"); facial_stripes for Tamiops/Sundasciurus/Callosciurus (Heaney 1985 says no other callosciurine has facial stripes, which conflicts with the pale cheek stripes of Tamiops, so that statement was not used); pale_dorsal_stripes absent for Sundasciurus (no source states it for all species).
